title: Next Gen Initiative 2026: Fellowship for Young African Women – Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Center
summary: Are you a young African woman passionate about public leadership, governance, development, gender, health, law, or public policy ? The Next Gen Initiative 2026 is an opportunity for emerging women leaders from selected African countries to strengthen their leadership skills, gain practical public leadership experience, and build networks for lasting impact. The Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Presidential Center for Women and Development (EJS Center) is launching the Next Gen Initiative, its flagship leadership program for emerging African women leaders. The 12-month fellowship is designed to prepare promising young women for future leadership roles through leadership development, mentorship, immersive learning, and hands-on public leadership placements alongside Amujae Leaders . Next Gen Initiative 2026 Fellowship The program aims to cultivate Africa s next generation of women public leaders by providing fellows with the exposure, experience, mentorship, and support needed to advance their leadership journeys. Throughout the 12-month fellowship, participants will have opportunities to: Develop leadership and professional skills Receive mentorship from experienced women leaders Gain practical exposure to public leadership Participate in immersive learning experiences Build professional networks across Africa Work alongside Amujae Leaders Strengthen their capacity to drive social and public impact Develop perspectives and skills to contribute to positive change in their communities and countries Who Can Apply? The Next Gen Initiative is seeking purpose-driven young African women who demonstrate leadership potential and a strong commitment to public service. Applicants should demonstrate: Integrity and strong ethical values Leadership potential Curiosity and willingness to learn Resilience and determination A strong commitment to public service A clear interest in advancing positive change in their communities and countries A commitment to developing their long-term leadership trajectory Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for the Next Gen Initiative 2026 , applicants must: Be 25–35 years old as of October 1, 2026 . Hold an undergraduate degree . Have at least three years of relevant and consistent professional experience . Have professional experience in public policy, law, development, gender, health, governance, or a related field . Demonstrate strong leadership potential, integrity, and commitment to public service. Show a clear interest in developing their leadership trajectory and contributing to positive change in their country and across Africa. Eligible Countries The inaugural Next Gen Initiative cohort is open only to citizens of the following countries : 🇰🇪 Kenya 🇱🇸 Lesotho 🇱🇷 Liberia 🇳🇬 Nigeria 🇸🇱 Sierra Leone Applicants from countries outside this list are not eligible for the inaugural cohort. Fellowship Duration The Next Gen Initiative is a 12-month fellowship program combining leadership development, mentorship, learning opportunities, and practical public leadership experience. Fellowship Stipend and Support Selected fellows will receive a monthly stipend for the duration of the 12-month fellowship to support their participation in the program. The fellowship therefore provides both professional development and financial support to help selected participants fully engage in the program. Why Apply for the Next Gen Initiative? The Next Gen Initiative offers emerging African women leaders an opportunity to gain practical leadership experience, mentorship, professional networks, and exposure to public leadership . For women seeking careers in government, public policy, development, governance, gender equality, health, law, or other public service fields , the fellowship can provide valuable experience and connections to support their leadership journey. APPLY NOW: Next Gen Initiative Application Form How to Apply for the Next Gen Initiative 2026 Eligible candidates are encouraged to complete the Next Gen Initiative Application Form and provide the required information demonstrating their leadership experience, professional background, commitment to public service, and aspirations for positive change. Next Gen Initiative 2026 – Quick Facts Category Details Program Next Gen Initiative Organization Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Presidential Center for Women and Development Duration 12 months Target group Emerging African women leaders Age 25–35 years as of October 1, 2026 Education Undergraduate degree Experience At least 3 years of relevant professional experience Eligible countries Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone Focus areas Leadership, public service, governance, development, policy and related fields Financial support Monthly stipend Program components Mentorship, leadership development, immersive learning and public leadership placements Next Gen Initiative Application Form If you are an eligible young woman from Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Nigeria, or Sierra Leone with a strong commitment to public service and leadership, this fellowship could be an important step in your leadership journey. title: COY21 2026: Global Youth Climate Conference in Türkiye – Delegate Applications Now Open
summary: Are you a young climate leader looking to participate in global climate discussions and contribute to the youth agenda ahead of COP31 ? Applications are now open for the 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change (COY21) , taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 5–7 November 2026 . Organized by YOUNGO , the official Children and Youth Constituency of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) , COY21 will bring together young people from around the world to build capacity, strengthen climate advocacy, develop practical skills, and contribute to the global youth climate agenda ahead of COP31. What Is COY21? The Conference of Youth (COY) is the world s largest and most significant gathering of children and young people focused on climate change. COY serves as an important preparatory space for young people before the annual UN Climate Change Conference. Through workshops, training, discussions and advocacy activities, participants develop the knowledge and skills needed to engage meaningfully in international climate policy processes. COY21 2026 will provide young people with opportunities to: Build knowledge and leadership skills on climate change. Participate in climate advocacy and youth diplomacy. Engage in negotiation-aligned sessions ahead of COP31. Share local and regional perspectives on climate challenges. Contribute to the global youth climate agenda. Connect with young climate leaders from around the world. Prepare collectively for participation in the COP31 process. COY21 Delegate Opportunity 2026 Applications are now being invited from motivated young leaders interested in joining the COY21 Delegation . Selected delegates will represent their communities, countries or regions, participate in international youth climate diplomacy, and contribute to shaping global youth priorities ahead of COP31 . Who Can Apply? To be eligible for the COY21 Delegate opportunity , applicants must: Be under 35 years old at the time of COY21. Demonstrate an interest in or engagement with climate action, youth leadership or policy advocacy at local, regional or international level. Commit to participating actively in pre- and post-COY21 delegation preparations, meetings and follow-up activities . Be able to self-fund travel to Antalya, Türkiye . CLICK HERE TO APPLY What Are COY21 Delegates Expected to Contribute? COY21 is seeking diverse, passionate and engaged young people who can: Represent their community, country or region internationally. Bring strong local perspectives to COY21 discussions and outcomes. Contribute to climate justice, climate policy and grassroots climate action . Share experiences and perspectives from their communities. Take knowledge, connections and commitments from COY21 back home to strengthen climate action. Diversity and Representation The final selection process will seek to ensure balanced representation across gender, geographic regions and thematic expertise . This means young people from diverse backgrounds and with different experiences in climate action, policy, advocacy and grassroots work are encouraged to apply. Important Application Requirement The use of AI to complete the application form is prohibited. Applications may be disqualified if it is determined that AI was used to complete the form. Applicants should therefore ensure that their responses accurately reflect their own experiences, perspectives and ideas. COY21 2026 Key Details Opportunity COY21 Delegate Event 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change Location Antalya, Türkiye Dates 5–7 November 2026 Age limit Under 35 Focus Climate action, youth leadership, advocacy and policy Travel Self-funded Deadline 5 September 2026 How to Apply for COY21 2026 Young climate leaders interested in joining the COY21 delegation should submit their Expression of Interes t before the deadline. Application deadline: 5 September 2026 For questions about the application or delegation, contact: liaisons@climatecoy.com admin@climatecoy.com Frequently Asked Questions What is COY21? COY21 is the 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change, bringing young people together ahead of COP31 to build capacity, advocate for climate action and contribute to the global youth climate agenda. Where will COY21 2026 take place? COY21 will take place in Antalya, Türkiye , from 5–7 November 2026 . Who can apply for the COY21 delegation? title: International Coproduction Fund (IKF) 2026: Funding Opportunity for International Music, Dance and Theatre Projects
summary: The Goethe-Institut International Coproduction Fund (IKF) supports international artistic collaborations that bring creators from different cultural backgrounds together to develop innovative productions and new approaches to intercultural exchange. The fund is designed to encourage international coproduction, cultural dialogue, artistic collaboration and the development of new creative networks within a global context. The 2026 application period for the current funding round runs from 17 August to 12 October 2026 . About the International Coproduction Fund The International Coproduction Fund supports collaborative projects involving international partners, with a particular focus on productions that encourage meaningful cultural exchange. The fund aims to create opportunities for artists and cultural practitioners to work across borders, exchange ideas and develop innovative artistic projects together. Supported areas include: Music Dance and theatre The programme encourages applicants to develop projects that demonstrate genuine international collaboration rather than simply presenting an existing production in another country. What the Fund Supports The International Coproduction Fund focuses on international coproductions that demonstrate partnership-based and dialogue-oriented approaches. Projects should contribute to: International cultural exchange Collaboration between artists and cultural practitioners Development of new artistic networks Innovative production methods Intercultural dialogue New approaches to international artistic cooperation Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate how their proposed project will benefit from the collaboration between international partners and how the partnership will contribute to the artistic development of the production. 2026 Application Round From 2026, the Goethe-Institut has confirmed two application periods. The second application round runs from mid-August until 12 October 2026 at 23:59 CET . Projects submitted during this round should be scheduled to: Start: January 2027 End: 31 December 2027 Applicants are encouraged to regularly check the Goethe-Institut website for any updates concerning the application process and requirements. APPLY HERE Inclusion and Accessibility The Goethe-Institut is committed to making cultural activities accessible to people with disabilities and strongly encourages artists with disabilities to apply. Accessibility-related costs connected to eligible projects will be covered by the fund. This provides an important opportunity for applicants to incorporate accessibility considerations into their project planning without having to treat accessibility costs as an additional barrier to participation. Sustainability The International Coproduction Fund also places importance on sustainability. Applicants are encouraged to consider how their projects can be planned and delivered in an environmentally responsible way. The Goethe-Institut can provide advice to applicants on how to incorporate environmentally friendly approaches into their projects. Application Deadline The deadline for the second 2026 application round is: 12 October 2026 at 23:59 CET Projects submitted during this round should begin from January 2027 and run through 31 December 2027 . Visit HERE to learn more about the International Coproduction Fund (IKF) 2026 Contact For questions concerning the International Coproduction Fund, applicants can contact: Goethe-Institut e.V. International Coproduction Fund (IKF) Email: koproduktionsfonds@goethe.de Conclusion The International Coproduction Fund (IKF) provides an opportunity for artists and cultural practitioners to develop international music, dance and theatre productions through meaningful cross-border collaboration. The programme places particular emphasis on international cultural exchange, innovative artistic production, intercultural cooperation and the creation of new networks . Applicants interested in developing collaborative artistic projects for 2027 should review the fund s requirements carefully and submit their applications before the 12 October 2026 deadline . title: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board of Directors 2026: Call for Expressions of Interest and Nominations
summary: The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is inviting expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals who may be considered for appointment to its Board of Directors . The opportunity provides individuals with an interest and experience in conservation, biodiversity protection, sustainable development and regional environmental governance with an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of an important Caribbean environmental fund. The proposed Board appointment will run for a maximum of two years , with the proposed term beginning on 1 October 2026 . Applications and nominations must be submitted by 7 September 2026 . About the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is a regional environmental fund established to provide stable, long-term financial resources for conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean. The Fund plays a role in supporting long-term approaches to environmental conservation and sustainable development throughout the region. Its work involves the mobilization and management of financial resources intended to support biodiversity and ecosystem-related priorities. As a regional institution handling resources for environmental and conservation purposes, effective governance and oversight are important to ensuring that the Fund operates responsibly and achieves meaningful strategic impact. It is within this context that the CBF Governance Committee has opened a formal call for individuals who may be considered for vacant positions on its skills-based Board of Directors. CBF Board of Directors Opportunity The CBF is seeking expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals for possible appointment to its Board of Directors. The Board is described as skills-based , meaning that the selection process is intended to identify individuals whose knowledge, experience and professional capabilities can contribute to the governance and strategic oversight of the Fund. The appointment is proposed for a maximum period of: Two years Proposed start date: 1 October 2026 Application deadline: 7 September 2026 The opportunity is therefore intended for individuals who are interested in contributing at a governance and strategic level to a regional organization focused on biodiversity conservation and environmental financing. Why Serve on the CBF Board? Serving on the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board provides an opportunity to contribute directly to the governance and strategic development of a regional institution working on biodiversity and conservation. According to the opportunity announcement, Board members can contribute to several important areas. 1. Help Shape the Strategic Direction of the CBF Directors will have an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund. Board-level participation can therefore involve contributing perspectives and expertise that help guide the institution s priorities and long-term development. The Board plays an important role in ensuring that the Fund continues to develop in a way that supports its conservation and biodiversity objectives. 2. Support Strong Governance The CBF is seeking Board members as part of efforts to ensure: Robust fiduciary oversight Objective governance Strategic impact This makes Board participation particularly important because the Fund is responsible for managing resources intended to support environmental and conservation priorities. Directors can contribute to the governance structures and oversight needed to support responsible institutional decision-making. 3. Contribute to Regional Conservation The CBF s work is focused on conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean. Board members therefore have the opportunity to contribute to an institution whose activities are connected to some of the region s broader environmental priorities. The position provides an opportunity to support efforts aimed at protecting biodiversity and strengthening long-term financing for conservation. 4. Engage With Regional and International Partners Board service can also provide opportunities for Directors to engage with partners working in conservation and sustainable development. The announcement notes that Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF at: Regional meetings International meetings Convenings Other strategic engagements Where appropriate, these engagements may also involve travel. This can provide Board members with opportunities to participate in discussions involving Caribbean and international partners committed to conservation and sustainable development. Nature of the Board Appointment The CBF Board opportunity is different from a conventional employment position. Board service is voluntary and does not carry remuneration . This means individuals appointed to the Board should understand that they will not receive a salary or regular remuneration for their Board service. However, Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF through regional and international engagements, including meetings and other strategic activities. The announcement specifically notes that travel may be involved where appropriate. Appointment Term The proposed appointment is for a maximum of two years . The proposed commencement date is: 1 October 2026 Applicants should therefore be prepared for the possibility of serving on the Board during the proposed two-year period, subject to the terms and conditions of the appointment. Therefore, applicants should carefully review the official application materials and nomination process for any additional requirements that may apply. It also does not provide a specific race or ethnicity requirement. title: Mission 44 Trustee Board Members Opportunity 2026: Apply for a Leadership Role in Driving Social Change
summary: Mission 44 is inviting experienced, passionate and purpose-driven individuals to join its Trustee Board and contribute to an organisation committed to empowering young people and tackling social injustice. The organisation is currently recruiting Trustee Board Members as part of its efforts to strengthen its leadership and governance while advancing its mission of creating meaningful opportunities and positive change for young people. This is an opportunity for individuals who have strong professional experience, a commitment to social impact and the ambition to contribute at a board level to an organisation focused on transforming young lives. The role is unremunerated , meaning trustees will not receive a salary for their board service. The application deadline is September 13, 2026 . The organisation brings together a diverse Board, staff team and Youth Advisory Board. This diversity is intended to provide the breadth of perspectives, experiences and ideas needed to drive meaningful and potentially radical change. Mission 44 says it welcomes applications from all sections of society and is particularly interested in candidates from underrepresented groups . The organisation is therefore looking for people who combine strong skills and experience with a genuine passion for transforming young lives and a positive, solution-oriented approach to social change. Mission 44 Trustee Board Members Opportunity The current vacancy is for Trustee Board Members within Mission 44 s Impact function. Trustees play an important role in the governance and strategic direction of an organisation. While the information provided does not specify individual trustee responsibilities in detail, the position is part of Mission 44 s leadership and governance structure. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to contribute their knowledge, professional expertise and perspective to an organisation working to empower young people and address social injustice. The organisation specifically highlights its interest in candidates who can bring diverse perspectives and those from groups that are currently underrepresented. Potential applicants should, therefore, consider applying if they can demonstrate a strong combination of Professional expertise relevant to organisational leadership, governance, strategy, impact or related areas. Strong judgement and strategic thinking that can contribute to board-level discussions and decision-making. A collaborative approach to working with other Board members, staff and young people. An understanding of diversity and inclusion and the importance of bringing different perspectives into organisational decision-making. Passion and optimism about creating meaningful and sustainable change. Mission 44 s recruitment message indicates that it is looking beyond technical qualifications alone. Diversity and Inclusion One of the notable aspects of this recruitment is Mission 44 s explicit encouragement of applications from across society. The organisation states that it welcomes applications from all sections of society , while particularly encouraging candidates from underrepresented groups . This means prospective applicants should not assume that they are excluded simply because they do not fit a traditional profile for board leadership. Instead, candidates should focus on the skills, experience, perspectives and values they can contribute to Mission 44 s mission. Is the Mission 44 Trustee Role Paid? The Trustee Board Member position is listed as unremunerated . This means candidates should not apply expecting a salary or conventional employment compensation for serving as a trustee. Instead, the opportunity is primarily suited to individuals who are interested in contributing their expertise, leadership and experience to a social-impact organisation and helping advance its mission. Applicants should therefore consider the role as a governance and impact opportunity rather than a conventional paid employment position. Why Consider the Mission 44 Trustee Opportunity? There are several reasons why experienced professionals may want to consider this opportunity. 1. Contribute to youth empowerment Mission 44 is focused on empowering young people and helping them overcome social injustice. Serving on its Board provides an opportunity to contribute to that mission at a strategic level. 2. Use your professional experience for social impact Individuals with significant experience in areas relevant to governance, strategy, impact, communications, finance, law, fundraising, organisational development or other disciplines may be able to use their expertise to support the organisation s work. 3. Contribute to strategic leadership Trustees have an important role in helping organisations maintain strong governance and make sound strategic decisions. This can provide an opportunity for experienced professionals to contribute beyond their normal organisational responsibilities. 4. Bring a different perspective Mission 44 is particularly interested in candidates from underrepresented groups. Individuals with different lived experiences, professional backgrounds and perspectives can help strengthen board-level conversations and contribute to more inclusive decision-making. 5. title: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026: Free Technical Support, 800 Hours of Development and Open Source Transformation for Nonprofits
summary: The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offering a valuable opportunity for selected nonprofit organizations to transform their existing software and technology projects into publicly accessible, licensed and well-documented open source tools — at no cost to participating organizations. The partnership brings together Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward to support a small group of technology-focused nonprofits with the technical expertise, student developer capacity and industry mentorship needed to prepare software for open source use or strengthen projects that are already part of the open source ecosystem. As part of the program, each selected nonprofit will receive a dedicated team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers who will work on the organization s project for 16 weeks . The program represents approximately 800 hours of technical work per team , supported by weekly check-ins, technical guidance, project management assistance and team coaching. The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have developed useful technology but lack the time, staff capacity or specialised expertise required to properly license, document, package and maintain that technology as an open source resource. Applications for the program close on September 9, 2026 . Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026 at a Glance Program: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Organizing partners: Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward Target applicants: Selected technology-focused nonprofit organizations Project focus: Open sourcing an existing nonprofit software tool or contributing to an existing open source project Technical support: Eight college student volunteer developers per nonprofit Program duration: 16 weeks Technical contribution: Approximately 800 hours per team Industry mentorship: Bloomberg employee volunteers Open source guidance: CodeDay Program support: Develop for Good Cost: No cost to participating nonprofits Nonprofit application deadline: September 9, 2026 Selection notification: October 2, 2026 Program kickoff: October 25, 2026 Final delivery: February 20, 2027 What Is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership? Many nonprofit organizations build or use technology to deliver their missions, but creating software and preparing it for open source distribution are two different challenges. A nonprofit may have an existing application, platform, internal tool or other technology that could potentially benefit other organizations. However, making that technology genuinely open source involves much more than publishing code online. The organization may need to address: Software licensing Technical documentation Code organization Developer onboarding Project contribution processes Technical maintenance User documentation Open source best practices Project management Quality assurance Collaboration with external developers These tasks require time and specialised technical knowledge that many nonprofits may not have available internally. The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is designed to help close this gap. Through the partnership, participating organizations receive a dedicated team of student developers and support from experienced professionals who can help turn an existing technology project into a more accessible and reusable open source resource. Who Is Behind the Program? The initiative is a collaboration between four organizations: Bloomberg Bloomberg is participating in the partnership through employee volunteers who will provide guidance and mentorship to participating nonprofit projects. Develop for Good Develop for Good provides the student development teams and program support. The organization will run weekly check-ins with participating students and provide structured support covering technical work, project management and team coaching. CodeDay CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices , helping participating nonprofits understand how to prepare their projects for open source use. Fast Forward Fast Forward is also part of the partnership, contributing to an initiative designed to strengthen technology capacity within the nonprofit sector. Together, these organizations provide a combination of student technical talent, professional mentorship, open source expertise and program management support. What Will Selected Nonprofits Receive? Selected organizations will receive several forms of support throughout the 16-week program. 1. A Dedicated Team of Eight Student Developers Each participating nonprofit will receive a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers . The students will dedicate their time to the nonprofit s selected project throughout the 16-week program. This gives nonprofits access to a substantial pool of technical capacity without the financial cost associated with hiring a conventional software development team. 2. Approximately 800 Hours of Technical Work The program estimates that each team will contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work . This can provide significant development capacity for a nonprofit that may otherwise struggle to dedicate internal resources to an open source initiative. The exact nature of the work will depend on the organization s project and the objectives established for the program. Potential work could involve preparing an existing tool for open source publication, improving documentation or contributing to an existing open source project. 3. Weekly Program Check-Ins Develop for Good will conduct weekly check-ins with students throughout the program. These check-ins are designed to help teams remain focused, address challenges and maintain progress toward the project s objectives. 4. Technical Support Participating teams will receive structured technical support to help them move their projects forward. This can be especially valuable for organizations that have a strong mission and a useful technology product but do not have extensive internal software engineering capacity. 5. Project Management Support The partnership also includes project management assistance. This helps keep the work organized and ensures that the student development team and nonprofit point-of-contact remain aligned on priorities, deliverables and timelines. 6. Team Coaching Teams will receive coaching designed to support effective collaboration and project execution. Because the program involves nonprofit staff, student developers and industry mentors, structured coaching can help ensure that different participants remain coordinated throughout the 16-week engagement. 7. Open Source Best-Practices Guidance CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices. This is particularly important for nonprofits that are making the transition from an internally developed or privately maintained tool to a publicly accessible project. 8. Bloomberg Employee Mentorship Participating nonprofits will receive weekly guidance from experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers. These mentors are described as being invested in the success of the projects and can provide an additional professional perspective throughout the program. 9. A Publicly Accessible and Documented Final Product One of the most important outcomes is a finished project that is intended to be: Publicly accessible Properly licensed Documented Ready for the nonprofit to use Potentially useful to other organizations This can extend the impact of a nonprofit s technology beyond its immediate internal use. What Does Open Source Mean for Participating Nonprofits? Open source software is software whose source code is made available under a license that allows others to access, use and, depending on the license, modify and redistribute it under defined conditions. For a nonprofit, making a tool open source can create opportunities for other organizations, developers and communities to benefit from technology that might otherwise remain limited to the organization that originally developed it. However, simply uploading software to a public repository does not necessarily mean that a project is ready for meaningful open source collaboration. A well-prepared open source project generally needs appropriate licensing, clear documentation and enough structure for other users or developers to understand how the project works and how they can engage with it. That is the gap this partnership is intended to address. Learn more HERE What Types of Projects Can Participate? The program is designed for nonprofits with an existing technology project that is ready to be open sourced or that needs support to contribute to an existing open source project. A nonprofit may therefore consider applying if it has: An existing software tool it wants to make open source A technology project that needs improved documentation A software project that needs preparation for public release An existing open source project that requires development support A technical project that could benefit from a dedicated student development team The organization should have a sufficiently defined project for the student developers and mentors to work on during the 16-week program. Apply HERE What Does the Nonprofit Need to Contribute? Although the program is offered at no cost to participating organizations, selected nonprofits are expected to commit time and resources in the form of staff participation. Each participating nonprofit should plan for approximately: 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks from a designated point-of-contact. The nonprofit point-of-contact will participate in activities such as: Regular check-ins Providing feedback Collaborating with student developers Working with industry mentors Answering project-related questions Helping clarify priorities Reviewing project progress Supporting decision-making when necessary This commitment is important because the student developers and mentors need a knowledgeable representative from the nonprofit to provide context and feedback. How Much Time Should a Nonprofit Expect to Commit? The stated commitment is approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks . Over the entire program period, this represents approximately 32–48 hours of point-of-contact involvement. Organizations should therefore select someone who can consistently participate throughout the program. A nonprofit that cannot provide a reliable point-of-contact may struggle to take full advantage of the technical resources being provided. What Does the Program Cost? The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offered at no cost to participating organizations . This is one of the program s major advantages because nonprofits can receive substantial technical support without having to pay for a professional software development team. The program combines volunteer student developers with industry mentors and structured organizational support to provide the technical capacity needed to advance participating projects. Why Open Source Can Matter for Nonprofits Transforming nonprofit software into open source can have benefits beyond the immediate project. A well-documented and publicly accessible tool can potentially: Allow other nonprofits to use the technology. Encourage collaboration among developers. Reduce duplication of technology development. Create opportunities for external contributions. Increase the visibility of the organization s technical work. Make the software easier for other organizations to evaluate and adopt. Build a community around a useful technology project. Extend the impact of technology developed for a specific nonprofit mission. The potential impact depends on the quality of the project, the needs of the wider community and the nonprofit s ability to maintain and support the software after the program concludes. Program Timeline The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership has a defined timeline from application through final delivery. September 9, 2026 — Applications Close This is the deadline for nonprofit organizations to submit their applications. Organizations interested in participating should complete their application before this date. October 2, 2026 — Selected Nonprofits Notified Organizations selected to participate will be notified on this date. October 25, 2026 — Program Kickoff The program officially begins with the kickoff on October 25, 2026. This marks the beginning of the 16-week collaboration involving the nonprofit, student developers and mentors. February 20, 2027 — Final Delivery The program is scheduled to conclude with final delivery on February 20, 2027. By this stage, participating teams will have worked toward completing the agreed project objectives. How to Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Nonprofit organizations interested in participating should submit an application through the program s online application form. Application deadline: September 9, 2026. Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Before applying, organizations should make sure they understand the program requirements and can commit the necessary staff time for the entire 16-week period. How Nonprofits Can Prepare a Strong Application Although the provided information does not specify a detailed scoring rubric, organizations can prepare by clearly defining the project they want the program to support. 1. Identify the technology project Determine which existing tool or project you want the student development team to work on. The project should be sufficiently defined to explain what the team will be expected to accomplish. 2. Explain why the project should become open source Organizations should be prepared to explain the value of making their technology publicly accessible. Consider: Who could benefit from the software? What problem does the tool solve? Why would other organizations use it? What could an open source community contribute? How could open sourcing the project increase its impact? 3. Define the technical challenges Identify the areas where your organization needs support. These could include: Software development Documentation Open source preparation Technical improvements Contribution workflows Existing open source development A clear understanding of the project s technical needs can help the development team work more effectively. 4. Identify a reliable point-of-contact Choose a staff member or representative who can commit 2–3 hours each week for 16 weeks . The person should have enough knowledge of the project to answer questions and provide meaningful feedback. 5. Consider the project s sustainability Open sourcing a project is not necessarily the end of the work. Organizations should consider how the software will be maintained, documented and supported after the partnership ends. Thinking about sustainability in advance can help ensure that the project s results remain useful after February 2027. Who Should Apply? The opportunity is especially relevant to nonprofit organizations that have an existing technology or software project and want technical assistance to make it open source or contribute to an existing open source project. A strong potential applicant may be a nonprofit that: Has already built a software tool. Has an existing technology project. Wants to release its software as open source. Needs assistance with documentation. Wants to improve an existing open source project. Has limited internal technical capacity. Can provide a dedicated point-of-contact. Can commit 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks. Is prepared to collaborate closely with student developers and mentors. What the Program Does Not Provide Applicants should also understand the nature of the opportunity. This is not described as a cash grant or direct financial award to nonprofits. Instead, the core support comes in the form of: Volunteer software development Technical assistance Open source guidance Industry mentorship Project management support Team coaching A structured 16-week development engagement The primary value is therefore technical capacity and expertise rather than direct funding . Questions to Ask Before Applying Before submitting an application, a nonprofit should consider: Do we have an existing technology project? Is the project suitable for open source development? Are we prepared to make the project publicly accessible? Do we have a clear understanding of what technical work is required? Can we identify a point-of-contact? Can that person commit 2–3 hours every week for 16 weeks? Can our organization provide timely feedback to developers? Are we prepared to work collaboratively with college student developers? Can we engage with industry mentors? Do we have a plan for using or maintaining the project s output after the program concludes? If the answer to these questions is generally yes, the partnership may be worth considering. Frequently Asked Questions What is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership? It is a collaborative program involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward that provides selected nonprofits with technical assistance to turn an existing software tool into an open source project or contribute to an existing open source project. How many student developers does each nonprofit receive? Each participating nonprofit receives a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers . How long does the program last? The program runs for 16 weeks . How much technical work is provided? Each team is expected to contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work . Does the program charge participating nonprofits? No. The opportunity is provided at no cost to participating nonprofits . How much time must the nonprofit contribute? The nonprofit s designated point-of-contact should expect to contribute approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks . What will the nonprofit representative do? The point-of-contact will participate in check-ins, provide feedback and collaborate with student developers and industry mentors. Does the program help with open source best practices? Yes. CodeDay provides guidance on open source best practices. Will nonprofits receive professional mentorship? Yes. Experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers provide weekly guidance throughout the program. What happens at the end of the program? The program is scheduled to have its final delivery on February 20, 2027 . The intended outcome is a publicly accessible, licensed and documented project that the nonprofit can use and that may potentially be useful to other organizations. When is the application deadline? The nonprofit application deadline is September 9, 2026 . How do I apply? Applications are submitted through the online application form: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership application form Contact Information Organizations with questions about the program can contact: Michael Gabrielle Nonprofit Partnerships Manager Develop for Good Email: michael@developforgood.org Important Dates to Remember For convenience, applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Date Milestone September 9, 2026 Nonprofit applications close October 2, 2026 Selected nonprofits notified October 25, 2026 Program kickoff February 20, 2027 Final delivery The most immediate date for prospective applicants is September 9, 2026 , which is the application deadline. Conclusion The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership provides selected nonprofits with an opportunity to access significant technical development capacity without paying for it. Through a collaboration involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward, participating organizations can receive a dedicated team of eight college student developers, industry mentorship, open source guidance and structured project support. The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have already developed a software tool but lack the internal time or technical capacity needed to properly prepare it for open source use. Rather than simply publishing existing code, participating teams can work toward creating a project that is publicly accessible, appropriately licensed and documented for future use. The commitment from nonprofits is also clearly defined. Each organization should provide a point-of-contact who can dedicate approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks to check-ins, feedback and collaboration. This involvement will be important for ensuring that student developers understand the organization s mission, users and technical priorities. With applications closing on September 9, 2026 , eligible nonprofits should begin identifying a suitable project, establishing their technical needs and selecting a reliable point-of-contact as soon as possible. For nonprofits looking to expand the impact of their technology, improve an existing open source project or make an internally developed tool available to a wider community, this partnership offers an opportunity to gain technical expertise and development support without direct program costs. title: UNFPA Internship 2026 in New York with Stipend | Private Sector & Civil Society Internship
summary: Are you a graduate student, recent graduate, or aspiring international development professional looking to gain experience with the United Nations? The UNFPA Internship Programme 2026 offers an opportunity to work with the Private Sector and Civil Society Branch (PSCSB) at UNFPA Headquarters in New York, USA . The UNFPA Intern, Private Sector and Civil Society Branch internship is a 24-week, full-time, in-person opportunity focused on strategic partnerships, private-sector engagement, philanthropy, fundraising, research, due diligence, and global development. Application deadline: 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM (New York time). UNFPA Internship 2026 – Key Details Organisation: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) Position: Intern, Private Sector and Civil Society Branch Programme: UNFPA Internship Programme Duty Station: New York, USA Location: UNFPA Headquarters Duration: 24 weeks Working arrangement: Full-time, in person Contract type: Internship Closing date: 9 September 2026, 17:00 (America/New_York) Remuneration: No salary; eligible interns may receive a stipend Application: CV and motivation letter submitted by email About the UNFPA Private Sector and Civil Society Internship The selected intern will work under the direct supervision of a Strategic Partnership Specialist within UNFPA s Private Sector and Civil Society Branch. The intern will support the Corporations and Businesses and Foundations and Philanthropy teams. The role provides practical exposure to strategic partnership development, donor intelligence, resource mobilisation, corporate engagement and international development. A work plan will be agreed at the beginning of the internship, including specific achievements and learning opportunities. Regular progress meetings will provide opportunities for professional development and skills-building The Position: Under the direct supervision of The Strategic Partnership Specialist within the Private Sector and Civil Society Branch (PSCSB) the intern will support the branch team in the areas of the Corporations and Businesses and Foundation and Philanthropy teams in PSCSB. A work-plan with achievements for the duration of the Internship and learning opportunities will be agreed upon. Periodic progress meetings will lead to a beneficial environment for the Intern enhancing her/his skills and capacity in areas related to UNFPA’s mandate. About UNFPA and How You Can Make a Difference: UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies. You would be responsible for: Support to Strategic Intelligence Pipeline Development Prospect Mapping CRM Management: Conduct comprehensive prospect mapping for foundations, corporations, and wealth management entities ahead of major global engagements (such as UNGA, WEF, and WHA). Utilize the CRM system to track donor trends and map high-potential prospects, ensuring profiles detail financial projections and thematic alignment. Funding Opportunities: Track and manage Requests for Proposals (RFPs) to identify new strategic funding avenues for both direct funding and the Coalition for Reproductive Justice in Business (CRJB). Strategic Material Development: Provide input to the development of key partnership materials to introduce the organization to potential partners and convert interest into formal resource commitments. Deliverables include Donor Intelligence Briefs, Grant Briefings, Background Notes (BNs), and strategic investment cases. Global Event Support Partnership Stewardship High-Level Event Coordination: Support the planning of high-level bilateral meetings, side events, and roundtables by drafting Concept Notes, meeting agendas, and external outreach emails. Maintain active event invitation trackers, participant lists, and follow-up tools. Tier 1 Partnership Support: Provide support for the management of existing Tier 1 Corporate Partnerships. This includes preparing Monthly Meeting Notes, assisting with legal and agreement management, and documenting meeting outcomes. Risk Mitigation Due Diligence Risk Assessment: Support pre-screening evaluations and due diligence processes for prospective corporate and philanthropic partners to ensure strict institutional alignment. Framework Drafting: Support the drafting and implementation of Partnership Risk Mitigation Frameworks to safeguard organizational interests. Knowledge Management Capacity Building Internal Repositories: Maintain and organize centralized business intelligence systems, including databases of successful private sector proposals and site maps grouped by clustered themes. Capacity Building Assets: Support the development of training materials, guidance manuals, toolkits, and market analyses designed to decentralize internal knowledge and empower Regional and Country Office (RO/CO) staff. Performance Reporting: Assist in the preparation, editing, and finalization of the relevant analysis reports, including Quarterly Analysis Reports for the Foundations Philanthropies (F P) Qualifying for an Internship All interns must meet the following educational and other eligibility requirements: Educational requirements Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year; Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher); Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme. Other eligibility requirements Demonstrate interest in the field of development; Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds. You Have: Your Education: Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme, the final academic year of a first university degree programme, or have recently graduated with an advanced degree in Social Sciences, Public Administration, International Relations, Business Administration, Development Studies, or a similar field. Your Experiences: Fluency in English. Knowledge of other languages is an asset. Strong analytical and writing skills. Initiative, sound judgment and demonstrated ability to work harmoniously with staff members from different national and cultural backgrounds. Some experience in working with development agencies, including in volunteer capacity is preferred but not required. Learning Elements: Upon completion of the assignment, and depending on its duration, the Intern will gain the following knowledge assets: Increased understanding of the UNFPA and the Private Sector and Civil Society Branch within UNFPA Understand the UNFPA mandate and policies, including regional set-up Understand and familiarize with UNFPA Governance and Executive Board Understand UNFPA programme design and delivery mechanisms Understand the dynamics of operational and programme support and communications to the field, and at the level of HQ Learn UN technical language, working procedures, and coordination mechanisms Write and formulate substantive documents Network with UN colleagues Work experience as a team member in a multicultural setting Financial Aspects: Interns do not receive a salary or any other form of remuneration from UNFPA. The costs associated with an intern s participation in the programme must be assumed either by the nominating institution, which may provide the required financial assistance to its students, or by the students themselves, who will have to meet living expenses as well as make their own arrangements for accommodation, travel and other requirements. However, they receive a stipend to help cover basic daily expenses related to the internship, if not financially supported by any institution or programme, such as a university, government, foundation, or scholarship programme. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. In addition, applicants must have medical insurance for the duration of the internship. Proof of insurance will need to be submitted before the internship begins. UNFPA does not provide medical insurance for interns. UNFPA Work Environment: UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA s workforce click here to learn more. Disclaimer: UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants bank accounts. How to Apply Please email your applications including a comprehensive 2-page CV and motivation letter under 400 words to pscsb.office@unfpa.org . Due to the volume of applications received, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview. title: Global Schools Advocates Program 2026: Fully Supported Opportunity for Teachers Worldwide
summary: Are you a teacher or school leader passionate about education for sustainable development (ESD), climate action and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) ? The Global Schools Advocates Program 2026 is inviting educators from around the world to join a global community working to bring sustainable development into classrooms and school communities. The program provides free online training, mentorship, teaching resources, professional development opportunities and a global network of educators committed to creating a more sustainable world. 📍 Location: Online / Worldwide 🎓 Eligible: Primary and secondary school teachers worldwide 💰 Funding: Free program ⏰ Time commitment: Minimum 5 hours per week 📚 Training: 10–15 hours online 🎯 Focus: Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), SDGs sustainability 🏆 Benefits: Training, mentorship, global educator network, toolkit certificate 📅 Application Deadline: September 18, 2026 Global Schools Advocates Program 2026 The Global Schools Advocates Program is a cohort-based initiative designed for teachers and school leaders who want to integrate sustainable development into their teaching and school activities. The program supports educators in bringing topics such as sustainability, justice, inequality and the Sustainable Development Goals into classrooms and school communities. Developed using insights from more than 220 sustainable development experts and 40+ educators , the program provides participants with training, pedagogical resources and opportunities to connect with like-minded educators globally. Who Can Become a Global Schools Advocate? Global Schools Advocates are educators working at the: Pre-primary level Primary school level Secondary school level Participants act as local action planners , working with their school communities to introduce and strengthen education for sustainable development. What Does the Global Schools Advocates Program Include? 1. Free Online Training Selected educators complete an online training program focused on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) . The training introduces participants to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and provides practical ideas for integrating sustainable development into classroom teaching. The training is delivered online in an asynchronous format , with optional live lectures, and takes approximately 10–15 hours to complete. After successfully completing the training, participants receive the Global Schools Advocate title and Advocate Toolkit . 2. Introduce ESD to Your School Community Advocates introduce Education for Sustainable Development to students, teachers, departments and school leadership. This can include conducting an ESD workshop for colleagues and using Global Schools resources to introduce sustainable development topics to students. Educators can adapt the approach to their local school and community context . 3. Integrate Sustainable Development Into Teaching Participants use the Advocate Toolkit, lesson plans and activity guides to implement lessons and activities that help students understand sustainable development and take action. There is no requirement to follow a fixed curriculum . Advocates can adapt activities to their school s needs with support from the Global Schools team. 4. Join a Global Educator Community Advocates can participate in monthly professional development sessions , engage with educator mentors and exchange ideas with teachers from around the world. Participants are also encouraged to share their experiences and lessons learned with the Global Schools community. Benefits of the Global Schools Advocates Program Teachers accepted into the program receive: Free online training in sustainable development education Monthly online workshops and discussions Access to a global network of educators Opportunities to participate in conferences and showcase advocacy work A structured mentorship program A comprehensive Advocate Toolkit with 17+ supporting documents A formal Certificate of Completion Selected educators may also have opportunities to share their work at events including the International Conference on Sustainable Development, Vatican Youth Symposium and ECOSOC Youth Forum . Who Is Eligible to Apply? The Global Schools Advocates Program is open to teachers working at primary and secondary schools worldwide . Teachers participating through volunteering programs such as UN Volunteers, Fulbright and Teach for All may also be eligible. Applicants should: Be a primary or secondary school teacher Have a high level of English to complete the training and participate in the global network Be willing to commit at least 5 hours per week Have a passion for the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Climate Agreement Be willing to learn and engage with an international community of educators Be able to inspire and motivate other teachers and school staff Be interested in integrating sustainable development into their school community Previous experience with the SDGs is not required. FIND OUT MORE AND APPLY HERE How Much Time Does the Program Require? Participants are expected to dedicate a minimum of 5 hours per week to the program. This time can include learning, developing ideas with other educators, experimenting with sustainable development approaches in lesson plans and helping create a movement for sustainable development within the school. Global Schools Advocates Program 2026 Deadline The application deadline is: September 18, 2026 Teachers and school leaders interested in participating are encouraged to review the program requirements and supporting documents before submitting an application. How to Apply for the Global Schools Advocates Program Interested educators can apply online through the official application form: Apply Here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScYQcCjzCdm7k0xe03VxFF7clwOZvXNvdlZi8c2VjKhKDD91g/viewform?usp=dialog Applicants can also review the Terms of Reference, FAQ and Training Syllabus before applying. The program materials provide additional information about participant requirements, course content and expectations. Why This Opportunity Matters Education plays an important role in helping young people understand and respond to global challenges such as climate change, inequality and sustainable development . Through the Global Schools Advocates Program, educators receive practical resources and a global network to help bring these issues into classrooms and encourage students to become active contributors to a more sustainable future. title: UNFPA Global Internships — Paid Opportunities for Students and Graduates in Nairobi, Copenhagen, New York & Global Internship Roster
summary: Are you looking for a paid UN internship in international development ? Applications are now open for several UNFPA Internship Opportunities in 2026 , offering students and recent graduates the chance to gain hands-on experience working with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) . These internships provide valuable exposure to global development, humanitarian programmes, youth engagement, and supply chain operations , while allowing interns to work alongside experts addressing issues such as reproductive health, gender equality, population data, and youth empowerment . If you want to start a career in the United Nations system , these internships can be a strong stepping stone. Why Apply for a UNFPA Internship? The UNFPA Internship Programme is designed to provide talented students and young professionals with real-world experience in international development and UN operations. Benefits of UNFPA Internships Selected interns may receive: Monthly stipend (paid internship) Opportunity to work within the United Nations system Hands-on experience in programme management, research, policy, and operations Mentorship from experienced UN professionals Exposure to global development and humanitarian programmes Networking opportunities with professionals across the UN and international NGOs These internships are highly valuable for anyone pursuing careers in international development, global health, policy, research, humanitarian work, or public administration . UNFPA Internship Opportunities 2026 Below are the currently available UNFPA internships and internship rosters open for applications. Deadline varies with some deadlines in December 2026 1. UNFPA Private Sector and Civil Society Internship – New York The UNFPA Private Sector and Civil Society Internship offers students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain hands-on experience with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) at its headquarters in New York, USA . The internship focuses on strategic partnerships, private-sector engagement, philanthropy, fundraising, donor intelligence, due diligence and global development . Location: New York, USA Office: UNFPA Headquarters Contract Type: Internship Duration: 24 weeks Work Arrangement: Full-time, in person Stipend: Eligible interns may receive a stipend Application Deadline: 9 September 2026 Key Areas of Work Strategic intelligence and prospect mapping Corporate and philanthropic partnerships Funding opportunities and RFP tracking Donor research and CRM management High-level events and partnership coordination Corporate partnership support Partner due diligence and risk assessment Knowledge management and capacity building Research, analysis and preparation of strategic reports Who Can Apply? Applicants should be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme , be in the final academic year of a first university degree, or have recently graduated with an advanced degree in Social Sciences, Public Administration, International Relations, Business Administration, Development Studies or a related field. Strong analytical, writing and communication skills are required, while experience with development agencies is an advantage but not essential. How to Apply: Submit a two-page CV and motivation letter of no more than 400 words to pscsb.office@unfpa.org . Apply by: 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM (New York time) . 2. Successful applicants may be matched with internship openings across country offices, regional offices, and headquarters . Applicants should be final-year Bachelor s or Master s students or recent graduates in Futures Studies, International Development, Public Policy, Economics, Sociology, Demography, Development Studies, Data Science, International Relations or related fields. The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) works in more than 150 countries to improve reproductive health, promote gender equality, and empower young people. Through its programmes, UNFPA supports initiatives such as: Ending preventable maternal deaths Ending unmet need for family planning Ending gender-based violence and harmful practices Supporting youth leadership and demographic research Interning with UNFPA provides an opportunity to contribute to these global priorities while building a career in the international development sector .
